articles.title: Court Notes Apparent AI-Generated Errors in Court Reporter's Transcript
articles.content:
印第安纳州上诉法院威廉姆斯诉州案判决意见摘录（周四发布），主笔法官费利克斯撰文，首席法官塔维塔斯与布拉德福德法官联名参与：

虽然“审判记录很少甚至从未完美过”，Ben-Yisrayl诉州案，753 N.E.2d 649，662（印第安纳州2001年），但本案中的笔录远非最佳状态。

笔录存在多种类型的错误。大量拼写错误改变了证词、提问或异议的含义。参见例如，Tr. Vol. II at 137:18，144:10，147:10；Tr. Vol. III at 6:13。在某些情况下，证人和审判律师的姓名被错误记录。Tr. Vol. II at 220:5；Tr. Vol. III at 142:15–20，143:15，162:4–5。

笔录某处将一项动议（可能由州方提出）错误地归属于审判法院。Tr. Vol. II at 107–08。另一处将一项异议（可能由威廉姆斯提出）错误地归属于法警。Tr. Vol. II at 177:15。又一处将州方的结案陈词错误地归属于审判法院。Tr. Vol. III at 228:1。

这些错误以及其他未详述的错误虽使我们的审查复杂化，但并未实质性地阻碍我们对威廉姆斯上诉的审查。无论如何，我们提醒书记员，本院依赖笔录作为转录程序的真实准确陈述。参见印第安纳州上诉规则28(B)（“书记员应证明笔录准确无误。”）；另参见例如，Orr诉州案，277 N.E.3d 1262，No. 25A-CR-1786（印第安纳州上诉法院2026年3月6日）（备忘录）（指出类似错误），转移被驳回，280 N.E.3d 249（印第安纳州2026年）。

根据审查所见的错误类型，生成式人工智能似乎可能辅助了本笔录的制作。虽然人工智能可以提高效率并成为许多专业人士的高效工具，但使用此类系统的人员有责任进行校对并确保生成产品的准确性。

法律专家罗布·弗洛因德（@RobertFreundLaw）周四发现了这一问题，404 Media（萨曼莎·科尔）对此进行了报道。

原文首次发表于Reason.com。
articles.summary:
From the opinion Thursday in Williams v. State, by Indiana Court of Appeals Judge Felix, joined by Chief Judge Tavitas and Judge Bradford:

Although "[t]rial records are rarely if ever perfect," Ben-Yisrayl v. State, 753 N.E.2d 649, 662 (Ind. 2001), the Transcript in this case is far from the best.

The Transcript contains various types of errors. There are numerous typos that change the meaning of the testimony, question, or objection. See, e.g., Tr. Vol. II at 137:18, 144:10, 147:10; Tr. Vol. III at 6:13. In some instances, witnesses' and trial attorneys' names are reported incorrectly. Tr. Vol. II at 220:5; Tr. Vol. III at 142:15–20, 143:15, 162:4–5.

At one point in the Transcript, a motion, presumably made by the State, is attributed to the trial court. Tr. Vol. II at 107–08. At another point, an objection, presumably made by Williams, is attributed to the Bailiff. Tr. Vol. II at 177:15. At yet another point, the State's closing argument is attributed to the trial court. Tr. Vol. III at 228:1.

These errors, among others not described herein, complicated but did not substantially impede our review of Williams's appeal. Regardless, we remind the Court Reporter that this court relies on transcripts being true and accurate representations of the transcribed proceedings. See Ind. Appellate Rule 28(B) ("The Court Reporter shall certify the Transcript is correct."); see, e.g., Orr v. State, 277 N.E.3d 1262, No. 25A-CR-1786 (Ind. Ct. App. Mar. 6, 2026) (mem.) (identifying similar errors), trans. denied, 280 N.E.3d 249 (Ind. 2026).

Based upon the types of errors reviewed, it appears that generative artificial intelligence may have assisted with the preparation of this transcript. While AI can improve efficiency and be a productive tool for many professionals, it is incumbent upon those using such systems to proofread and ensure the accuracy of the generated product.

Rob Freund (@RobertFreundLaw) spotted this Thursday, and 404 Media (Samantha Cole) wrote about it.

The post Court Notes Apparent AI-Generated Errors in Court Reporter's Transcript appeared first on Reason.com.

articles.title: Brian Fitzpatrick Makes the Case for Callais
articles.content:
学术界似乎达成了共识，认为最高法院在路易斯安那州诉卡莱斯案中的裁决是错误的。但这究竟说明的是这个判决的问题，还是法学学术界的问题？布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克在SCOTUSBlog上发表了一篇题为“为卡莱斯案辩护”的文章，提出了这个问题。

菲茨帕特里克在文章开篇写道：

“本刊物收到了大量学术界对路易斯安那州诉卡莱斯案批评的文章，但没有发表过一篇为其辩护的文章。因此我决定在我的专栏中承担这个任务。毕竟，我相当确信大法官安东宁·斯卡利亚会认可这个判决。

正如你将看到的，我发现这个任务并不特别困难。这引发了一个问题：为什么没有其他人愿意为最高法院一项6票对3票的裁决辩护？”

这篇文章篇幅很短，你应该阅读全文。

这篇文章《布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克为卡莱斯案辩护》最先出现在Reason.com上。
articles.summary:
There appears to be an academic consensus that the Supreme Court's decision in Louisiana in Callais is incorrect. But does this tell us more about the decision or about the legal academy? Brian Fitzpatrick raises this question in a SCOTUSBlog essay "The Case for Callais."

Fitzpatrick's essay begins:

This publication has been inundated with essays by academics critical of Louisiana v. Callais, but has not published a single one in defense of it. So I decided to take it on in my column. After all, I am pretty sure Justice Antonin Scalia would have approved of the decision.

As you will see, I didn't find the assignment particularly difficult. Which raises a question: why has no one else been willing to defend a 6-3 decision of the Supreme Court?

The essay is short, and you should read the whole thing.

The post Brian Fitzpatrick Makes the Case for <i>Callais</i> appeared first on Reason.com.

articles.title: Is There Actually an Error in the Supreme Court's Analysis in Loper Bright?
articles.content:
周四，我注意到高级巡回法院法官雷·伦道夫在Hospital Menonita de Guayama诉NLRB案（该案本身也颇值得关注）中的异议里有一个有趣的脚注，暗示最高法院在洛珀Bright Enterprises诉Raimondo案中结束雪佛龙遵从原则时，未能考虑到雪佛龙案并非行政程序法案件，而是受清洁空气法第307条的司法审查条款管辖。但实际情况真是如此吗？

一位细心的读者向我提供了另一条脚注——这篇来自约翰·达菲教授的法学评论文章——文章表明，在雪佛龙诉NRDC案裁决时，法院面临的问题实际上受行政程序法管辖。达菲教授在第19条脚注中写道：

部分学术研究认为，雪佛龙案本身不受第706条约束，因为清洁空气法第307条第(d)款（42 U.S.C. § 7607(d)）包含明确豁免条款，使第706条不适用。参见，例如Jack M. Beermann, Chevron Is a Rorschach Test Ink Blot, 32 J.L. & POL. 305, 307–08, 307 n.8 (2017)（指出“根据清洁空气法对EPA规则进行的司法审查受42 U.S.C. § 7607(d)管辖，而非行政程序法第706条”）。然而，相关条款仅豁免第307(d)(1)条中列出的EPA行为适用第706条，当时该条包括EPA行为的十四个类别，均未涵盖雪佛龙诉讼中审查的EPA规则制定。参见42 U.S.C. § 7607(d)(1)(A)–(N) (1982)。事实上，EPA在制定雪佛龙案中受质疑的最终规则时，分析了第307条第(d)款的适用性，并正确认定相关规则“不受第307(d)条约束”。Requirements for Preparation, Adoption and Submittal of Implementation Plans, 46 Fed. Reg. 50766, 50770 (Oct. 14, 1981) (codified at 40 C.F.R. pts. 51–52).

因此，伦道夫法官或许言之过早。

这是一个有趣的争议，但对洛珀Bright Enterprises案影响不大。伦道夫法官的观点由请愿方提出（参见例如口头辩论笔录第87页），而42 U.S.C. § 7607下的司法审查实质与行政程序法第706条下的司法审查并无重大差异（尽管对于规则制定存在重要的程序差异）。

虽然雪佛龙案未提及行政程序法，但雪佛龙原则被认为适用于行政程序法案件，因此该原则是否符合行政程序法至关重要——这一点伦道夫法官也承认。最高法院在洛珀Bright案中的裁决驳回了雪佛龙方法论——特别是要求法院遵从机构对模糊Statute语言合理解释的规定——而非驳回其对清洁空气法的解释或认定EPA法规是可允许的。

《最高法院在洛珀Bright案中的分析是否存在实际错误？》一文首次发表于Reason.com。
articles.summary:
On Thursday, I noted an interesting footnote in Senior Circuit Judge Ray Randolph's dissent in Hospital Menonita de Guayama v. NLRB (an interesting decision in its own right), suggesting that the Supreme Court's decision ending Chevron deference in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimando failed to account for the fact that Chevron had not been an APA case, but was rather governed by the judicial review provisions of the Clean Air Act. But is this so?

An astute reader pointed me to another footnote--this one from a law review article by Professor John Duffy--suggesting that at the time Chevron v. NRDC was decided, the issue from the Court was, in fact, governed by the APA. In FN19, Professor Duffy writes:

Some scholarship suggests that the Chevron case itself was not subject to section 706 because subsection (d) of section 307 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. § 7607(d)) contains an explicit exemption making section 706 inapplicable. See, e.g., Jack M. Beermann, Chevron Is a Rorschach Test Ink Blot, 32 J.L. &POL. 305, 307–08, 307 n.8 (2017) (stating that "[j]udicial review of EPA rules under the Clean Air Act is governed by 42 U.S.C. § 7607(d) and not by APA § 706"). The relevant provision, however, exempts from section 706 only EPA actions listed in section 307(d)(1), which at the relevant time included fourteen categories of EPA actions, none of which covered the EPA rulemaking being reviewed in the Chevron litigation. See 42 U.S.C. § 7607(d)(1)(A)–(N) (1982). In fact, at the time it was promulgating the final rule challenged in Chevron, the EPA itself analyzed the applicability of subsection (d) of section 307 and correctly determined that rules being promulgated were "not subject to Section 307(d)." Requirements for Preparation, Adoption and Submittal of Implementation Plans, 46 Fed. Reg. 50766, 50770 (Oct. 14, 1981) (codified at 40 C.F.R. pts. 51–52).

So perhaps Judge Randolph spoke too soon.

This is an interesting dispute, but it does not have much bearing on Loper Bright Enterprises. Judge Randolph's point was raised by the petitioners (see, e.g,, the oral argument transcript at p. 87), and the substance of judicial review under 42 U.S.C. § 7607 is not materially different from that under APA § 706 (though there are important procedural differences for rulemakings).

While Chevron made no reference to the APA, the Chevron doctrine was understood to apply to APA cases, so whether the doctrine comports with the APA mattered--a point Judge Randolph concedes. The Court's decision in Loper Bright rejected the Chevron methodology--in particular the requirement that courts defer to reasonable agency interpretations of ambiguous statutory language--not its interpretation of the Clean Air Act or its conclusion that the EPA regulation at issue was permissible.

The post Is There Actually an Error in the Supreme Court's Analysis in <i>Loper Bright</i>? appeared first on Reason.com.
